sections.heading: Lead
History
sections.wikitext:
Hank Ballard wrote "The Twist" after seeing teenagers in Tampa, Florida, doing the dance, [[Twist (dance)|the twist]].<ref>Bronson, Fred (2003). ''The Billboard Book of Number One Hits'', p.74. {{ISBN|9780823076772}}.</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Eury|first=Michael|date=August 2020 |title=The Twist|journal=RetroFan|publisher=[[TwoMorrows Publishing]] |location=United States|issue=10 |pages=16–17}}</ref> In a 2014 interview with Tom Meros, Midnighters member Lawson Smith claimed that The Gospel Consolaters' Nathaniel Bills wrote the song and initially asked [[The Spaniels]] to record it, and that Ballard "stole" the song, falsely claiming authorship.<ref>{{cite web |last=Meros |first=Tom |title=Midnighters' Lawson Smith: Hank Ballad Stole 'The Twist' |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-7eXm91EVms  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211222/-7eXm91EVms |archive-date=December 22, 2021 |url-status=live|website=[[YouTube]] |access-date=October 10, 2021 |date=October 29, 2014}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Green and Ballard already had written a song together called "Is Your Love for Real", which was based on [[Clyde McPhatter]] and [[The Drifters]]' 1955 song "[[What'cha Gonna Do (The Drifters song)|What'cha Gonna Do]]", so they created an entirely new song by simply putting the new Twist words to the older melody. They originally recorded a loose version of the song in a Florida studio for [[Vee-Jay Records]] in early 1958, with slightly different lyrics, featuring Green on guitar playing like [[Jimmy Reed]]. This version appeared on the box set "The Vee-Jay Story" in 1993, but it went unreleased at the time. They did not get around to recording the released version until November 11, 1958, when the Midnighters were in Cincinnati.{{cn|date=October 2021}}

Ballard thought "The Twist" was the hit side, but [[King Records (United States)|King Records]] producer [[Henry Glover]] preferred the ballad "Teardrops on Your Letter", which he had written himself.{{cn|date=October 2021}} The song ultimately became the [[A-side and B-side|B-side]] of Hank Ballard and The Midnighters' 1959 single "Teardrops on Your Letter".
sections.text:
Hank Ballard wrote "The Twist" after seeing teenagers in Tampa, Florida, doing the dance, the twist. In a 2014 interview with Tom Meros, Midnighters member Lawson Smith claimed that The Gospel Consolaters' Nathaniel Bills wrote the song and initially asked The Spaniels to record it, and that Ballard "stole" the song, falsely claiming authorship. Green and Ballard already had written a song together called "Is Your Love for Real", which was based on Clyde McPhatter and The Drifters' 1955 song "What'cha Gonna Do", so they created an entirely new song by simply putting the new Twist words to the older melody. They originally recorded a loose version of the song in a Florida studio for Vee-Jay Records in early 1958, with slightly different lyrics, featuring Green on guitar playing like Jimmy Reed. This version appeared on the box set "The Vee-Jay Story" in 1993, but it went unreleased at the time. They did not get around to recording the released version until November 11, 1958, when the Midnighters were in Cincinnati.{{cn|date=October 2021}}

Ballard thought "The Twist" was the hit side, but King Records producer Henry Glover preferred the ballad "Teardrops on Your Letter", which he had written himself.{{cn|date=October 2021}} The song ultimately became the B-side of Hank Ballard and The Midnighters' 1959 single "Teardrops on Your Letter".

The song became popular on a [[Baltimore]] television dance show hosted by local DJ [[Buddy Deane]]; Deane recommended the song to [[Dick Clark]], host of the national ''[[American Bandstand]]'', then based in [[Philadelphia]]. When the song proved popular with his audience, Clark attempted to book Ballard to perform on the show. Ballard was unavailable, and Clark searched for a local artist to record the song. He settled on Checker, whose voice was very similar to Ballard's.<ref name="behind">{{cite book |title=Behind The Hits:Inside Stories of Classic Pop and Rock and Roll |last=Shannon |first=Bob |author-link=Bob Shannon (WCBS-FM) |author2=John Javna  |year=1986 |publisher=Warner Books |location=New York |isbn=0-446-38171-3 |pages= 98–99}}</ref> Checker's version featured Buddy Savitt on saxophone and Ellis Tollin on drums,<ref name="MIX">{{cite web
 |last        = Jackson
 |first       = Blair
 |title       = Classic Tracks: Chubby Checker's "The Twist"
 |work        = Mix Magazine
 |date        = May 1, 2007
|url         = http://mixonline.com/recording/tracking/audio_chubby_checkers_twist/
 |url-status     = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20110629140731/http://mixonline.com/recording/tracking/audio_chubby_checkers_twist/
 |archive-date = June 29, 2011
}}</ref> with backing vocals by [[the Dreamlovers]]. Exposure for the song on ''American Bandstand'' and on  ''The Dick Clark Saturday Night Show'' helped propel the song to the top of the American charts.<ref name="stars">{{cite book|title= Rock Stars Encyclopedia|last= Rees|first= Dafydd|author2= Luke Crampton|year= 1999|publisher= DK Publishing|location= New York|isbn= 0-7894-4613-8|pages= [https://archive.org/details/rockstarsencyclo00rees/page/192 192–194]|url-access= registration|url= https://archive.org/details/rockstarsencyclo00rees/page/192}}</ref>

In July 1960, Checker performed "The Twist" for the first time in front of a live audience at the Rainbow Club in [[Wildwood, New Jersey]], and just weeks later, on August 6, 1960, the song became a national sensation after Checker performed it on Dick Clark's ''American Bandstand''. In Canada, his version was co-charted with the Hank Ballard version.

In late 1961 and early 1962, the twist craze belatedly caught on in high society. Sightings of celebrities doing the dance made the song a hit with adults, particularly after a report in the [[Igor Cassini|Cholly Knickerbocker]] gossip column. Soon there were long lines at the [[Peppermint Lounge]] nightclub in New York, the most popular celebrity twisting spot. This new interest made "The Twist" the first recording to hit number one on the United States charts during two separate chart runs, and marked a major turning point for adult acceptance of rock and roll music.<ref name="behind"/>

Checker re-recorded the song numerous times. An updated 1982 recording (from his album ''The Change Has Come'') was retitled "T-82", and in the 1990s, he recorded a [[country music|country]] version. In the late 1970s, he recorded a new version that, except for the sound mix and some minor arrangement changes, was identical to the 1960 original; as a result this later version is often misidentified on compilations as the original recording. In 1988, he joined [[The Fat Boys]] on a rap version of the song, which hit number 2 in the UK, number 16 in the US, and number 1 in Germany and Switzerland. Checker also joined the group to perform the song that summer at [[Nelson Mandela 70th Birthday Tribute|a London tribute concert]] for [[Nelson Mandela]].<ref name="stars" /> In addition, he recorded variations on the theme, such as "[[Let's Twist Again]]" to keep the craze alive ("Let's Twist Again" was and has remained more popular than "The Twist" itself in the United Kingdom). [[Joey Dee and the Starliters]], the Peppermint Lounge house band, scored a hit with "[[Peppermint Twist]]", while other artists, including [[Sam Cooke]] scored with other "Twist"-themed songs. In Europe, [[Petula Clark]] scored hits in several countries with "Twist"-themed records, while [[Bill Haley and His Comets]] recorded several albums of Twist songs in [[Mexico]] for the [[Orfeón (Mexican record label)|Orfeon Records]] label. In 1997, the song was featured in a Teledyne Waterpik commercial, and a commercial for [[Denny's]] in 1998, to promote the New Slams.

In the sixth episode of the second season of the TV series ''[[Quantum Leap (1989 TV series)|Quantum Leap]]'', entitled "Good Morning, Peoria" (set on September 9, 1959), Dr. Sam Beckett ([[Scott Bakula]]) and Al Calavicci ([[Dean Stockwell]]) meet Chubby Checker (played by himself) in a radio station, where they sing and dance "The Twist". An impressed Checker asks, "Can I use that move?" Sam responds, "Yah, but I got it from you!". The song was used in the 2007 film ''[[Spider-Man 3]]'' and appears on the film's [[Spider-Man 3 (soundtrack)|official soundtrack album]].

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
The Keil Isles recorded "The Twist" with David Dunningham as their producer. They also recorded the song "Siboney" which was also produced by Dunningham. With "The Twist" as the A side, both songs were released on [[Viking Records]] single VS.69. The single was credited to Herma Keil with the Keil Isles.45Cat - [https://www.45cat.com/record/vs69 Herma Keil With The Keil Isles - The Twist] [[Chubby Checker]]'s version of "The Twist" was deemed to too noisy for airplay by New Zealand's [[NZBS]]. This cleared the way for the [[Keil Isles]] to have success with their version.''Blue Smoke''
''The Lost Dawn of New Zealand Popular Music, 1918–1964''
By Chris Bourke · 2013 - {{ISBN|978-1-77558-027-0}} - [https://www.google.com/books/edition/Blue_Smoke/AUOdEQAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22Keil+Isles%22The+Twist%22&pg=PT698&printsec=frontcover Page unknown The NZBS decision -] As reported by Fred Gebbie in the New Zealand section of ''[[Billboard Music Week]]'' for the week of 10 March 1962, the Keil version of "The Twist" had topped the 18,000 mark.''Billboard Music Week'', March 10, 1962 - [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/60s/1962/Billboard%201962-03-10.pdf Page 23 NEW ZEALAND, ''Twist Still Going Full Blast in N.Z.'' By FRED GEBBIE] Their version outsold Chubby Checker's version in New Zealand.''Orlando Sentinel'', March 23, 1990 - [https://www.orlandosentinel.com/1990/03/23/music-a-driving-force-in-life-of-guitar-builder-from-samoa/ NEWS, MUSIC A DRIVING FORCE IN LIFE OF GUITAR BUILDER FROM SAMOA (UPDATED: July 27, 2021)]
sections.text:
The Keil Isles recorded "The Twist" with David Dunningham as their producer. They also recorded the song "Siboney" which was also produced by Dunningham. With "The Twist" as the A side, both songs were released on Viking Records single VS.69. The single was credited to Herma Keil with the Keil Isles.
Chubby Checker's version of "The Twist" was deemed to too noisy for airplay by New Zealand's NZBS. This cleared the way for the Keil Isles to have success with their version.

As reported by Fred Gebbie in the New Zealand section of Billboard Music Week for the week of 10 March 1962, the Keil version of "The Twist" had topped the 18,000 mark. Their version outsold Chubby Checker's version in New Zealand.

sections.heading: Airplay
sections.wikitext: As reported in the 17 February issue of ''Billboard Music Week'', Chubby Checker's rejected version of "The Twist" had finally been given air-time on New Zealand radio but that wasn't until the version by The Keil Isles had been plugged throughout New Zealand.<ref>''Billboard Music Week'', February 17, 1962 - [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/60s/1962/Billboard%201962-02-17.pdf Page 42 International News ● <u>''Continued from page 18''</u>]</ref>
sections.text: As reported in the 17 February issue of Billboard Music Week, Chubby Checker's rejected version of "The Twist" had finally been given air-time on New Zealand radio but that wasn't until the version by The Keil Isles had been plugged throughout New Zealand.

sections.heading: Billboard Music Week Hits Of The World, New Zealand
sections.wikitext: For the week of 17 February 1962, both The Keil Isles and Chubby Checker versions of "The Twist" had moved from No. 2 to No. 1 on the New zealand section of the ''Billboard Music Week'' Hits Of The World chart.<ref>''Billboard Music Week'', February 17, 1962 - [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/60s/1962/Billboard%201962-02-17.pdf Page 12 BILLBOARD MUSIC WEEK HITS OF THE WORLD, NEW ZEALAND, This Week 1, Last Week 2, THE TWIST-The Keil Isles/Chubby Checker (Viking/Top Rank)-Alberts]</ref> The following week, only the Chubby Checker version was showing on the chart.<ref>''Billboard Music Week'', February 24, 1962 - [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/60s/1962/Billboard%201962-02-24.pdf Page 22 BILLBOARD MUSIC WEEK HITS OF THE WORLD, NEW ZEALAND, This Week 2, Last Week 1, THE TWIST- Chubby Checker (Top Rank)- Alberts]</ref> For the week of 3 March, there was no New Zealand section shown.<ref>''Billboard Music Week'', March 3, 1962 - [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/60s/1962/Billboard%201962-03-03.pdf Page 12 BILLBOARD MUSIC WEEK HITS OF THE WORLD]</ref> For the week of 10 March with the New Zealand section included, both The Chubby Checker and Keil Isles versions had dropped down from No. 2 to No. 7.<ref>''Billboard Music Week'', March 19, 1962 - [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/60s/1962/Billboard%201962-03-10.pdf Page 21 BILLBOARD MUSIC WEEK HITS OF THE WORLD, NEW ZEALAND, This Week 7, Last Week 2 THE TWIST -Chubby Checker/Keil Isles (Top Rank-Viking)-Alberts]</ref>
sections.text: For the week of 17 February 1962, both The Keil Isles and Chubby Checker versions of "The Twist" had moved from No. 2 to No. 1 on the New zealand section of the Billboard Music Week Hits Of The World chart. The following week, only the Chubby Checker version was showing on the chart. For the week of 3 March, there was no New Zealand section shown. For the week of 10 March with the New Zealand section included, both The Chubby Checker and Keil Isles versions had dropped down from No. 2 to No. 7.

In 1988, American hip-hop trio Fat Boys covered "The Twist" with featured lyrics from Checker and additional rap lyrics written by Jim Glenn and Damon Wimbley. Produced by Albert Cabrera and Tony Moran (the Latin Rascals), this version reached number two in the United Kingdom and number one in West Germany, as well as number 16 on the Billboard Hot 100. The song's music video was produced by Ken Walz and shows the Fat Boys doing the twist with Checker at a sweet sixteen party. Checker initially missed the filming in May 1988 due to being hospitalized with spinal meningitis.

sections.heading: Certifications
Accolades
sections.wikitext:
Chubby Checker's "The Twist" held the honor of being the most successful single in ''Billboard'' history on its various "Greatest Hot 100 Songs of All Time" charts over the decades.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/chubby-checker-the-twist-hot-100-number-one/ |title=Chubby Checker's 'The Twist': The Improbable Life and Legacy of the Hot 100's All-Time Number One Song |date=August 2, 2018 |magazine=Billboard |access-date=August 14, 2018}}</ref> It held the title until 2021, when it was dethroned by the Weeknd's "[[Blinding Lights]]".<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Mamo|first=Heran|date=November 23, 2021|title=The Greatest Hit: The New No. 1 Song of All Time|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/features/the-weeknd-blinding-lights-billboard-cover-story-2021-interview-1235001282/|access-date=December 2, 2021|magazine=Billboard|language=en-US}}</ref>

The song was ranked number 451 on the ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' magazine's list of [[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Songs of All Time|The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time]] in 2004, and number 457 on the revised list in 2010. [[Jim Dawson]] wrote a 1995 book about the song and the Twist phenomenon called ''The Twist: The Story of the Song and Dance That Changed the World'' for [[Faber and Faber]].

In 2000, the 1960 recording by [[Chubby Checker]] on [[Parkway Records]] was inducted into the [[Grammy Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.grammy.com/awards/hall-of-fame-award#t|title=GRAMMY Hall Of Fame | Hall of Fame Artists | GRAMMY.com|website=grammy.com}}</ref>

The song has been added to the [[National Recording Registry]] in the [[Library of Congress]] on March 21, 2013, for long-term preservation.<ref>{{cite web |title=Simon & Garfunkel song among those to be preserved |url=http://www.cfnews13.com/content/news/cfnews13/news/article.html/content/news/articles/ap/2013/03/21/Simon__Garfunkel_song_among_those_to_be_preserved.html |publisher=CFN13 |access-date=March 21, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130410165726/http://www.cfnews13.com/content/news/cfnews13/news/article.html/content/news/articles/ap/2013/03/21/Simon__Garfunkel_song_among_those_to_be_preserved.html |archive-date=April 10, 2013}}</ref> In 2014, ''Billboard'' magazine declared the song the "biggest hit" of the 1960s.<ref name="BB2014">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6296373/billboard-hot-100-1960|title=The Top 20 ''Billboard'' Hot 100 Hits of the 1960s|last=Leight|first=Elias|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date=October 27, 2014|access-date=October 28, 2014}}</ref>

In 2018, Checker's version was one of six singles inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in a new category honoring singles by artists who have not been elected to the Hall.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cleveland.com/entertainment/index.ssf/2018/04/rock_and_roll_hall_of_fame_int.html|title=Rock and Roll Hall of Fame introduces new category for singles |last=Smith|first=Troy L.|date=April 15, 2018|website=Cleveland.com|access-date= April 21, 2018}}</ref>
sections.text:
Chubby Checker's "The Twist" held the honor of being the most successful single in Billboard history on its various "Greatest Hot 100 Songs of All Time" charts over the decades. It held the title until 2021, when it was dethroned by the Weeknd's "Blinding Lights".

The song was ranked number 451 on the Rolling Stone magazine's list of The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time in 2004, and number 457 on the revised list in 2010. Jim Dawson wrote a 1995 book about the song and the Twist phenomenon called The Twist: The Story of the Song and Dance That Changed the World for Faber and Faber.

In 2000, the 1960 recording by Chubby Checker on Parkway Records was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame.

The song has been added to the National Recording Registry in the Library of Congress on March 21, 2013, for long-term preservation. In 2014, Billboard magazine declared the song the "biggest hit" of the 1960s.

In 2018, Checker's version was one of six singles inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in a new category honoring singles by artists who have not been elected to the Hall.
